title: ज्योति समूहको अर्बौँ कर्जा दुरुपयोगमा दुई सरकारी बैंकको भूमिका शंकास्पद, छानबिनको दबाब
content:
काठमाडौं । ज्योति समूहका अध्यक्ष डा. रूप ज्योति र उनीसँग सम्बद्ध कम्पनीहरूले बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट लिएको अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ कर्जा गैरकानूनी रूपमा अन्यत्र प्रवाह गरी दुरुपयोग गरेको विषयमा दुई सरकारी बैंकको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न उठेको छ । महालेखापरीक्षकको कार्यालयले प्रतिवेदनमार्फत यो प्रकरणमा आधिकारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गर्दै नागरिकको बचत जोखिममा पारिएको र कर छली गरिएको निष्कर्ष निकालेपछि छानबिन गर्नुपर्ने स्थिति सिर्जना भएको हो । महालेखाको उक्त प्रतिवेदन अहिले संघीय संसद्को सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिमा पुगेको छ । प्रतिवेदनमा कर्जा दुरुपयोग र कर छलीमा संलग्न कम्पनीहरूको कारोबारलाई नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक ऐन, २०५८, बैंकिङ्ग कसुर तथा सजाय ऐन, २०६४ र आयकर ऐन, २०५८ का प्रचलित व्यवस्था अनुसार राज्यका अन्य अनुसन्धानकारी निकायहरूको सहयोग र समन्वयमा छानबिन गरी कारबाही गर्न सरकारलाई निर्देशन दिएको उल्लेख छ । यस कर्जा प्रकरणमा सरकारी स्वामित्वका दुई बैंकहरू राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंक र नेपाल बैंक जोडिएका छन् । महालेखाले यस विषयलाई बेरुजुका रूपमा समेत कायम गरेपछि सम्बन्धित कम्पनी, कर्जा लगानी गर्ने बैंक तथा नियामक निकायको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न उठेको छ । सामान्यतया, कुनै पनि कम्पनी वा संस्थालाई कर्जा प्रवाह गर्दा त्यसको लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदन मुख्य आधार हुन्छ । तर, ज्योति समूह सम्बद्ध कम्पनीका लेखापरीक्षकले राय दिन अस्वीकार गरेको विवादित लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदनकै आधारमा यी सरकारी बैंकहरूले कसरी अर्बौँ कर्जा स्वीकृत गरे भन्ने विषय बहसमा आएको छ । कमजोर धितो र लेखापरीक्षकले नै शंकास्पद ठहर्‍याएको प्रतिवेदन प्राप्त हुँदाहुँदै कर्जा दिनु र कर्जा दुरुपयोग भएको सार्वजनिक भइसक्दा पनि असुलीको ठोस प्रक्रियामा खेलेको भूमिकाका आधारमा यी दुई बैंकमाथी पनि छानबिन हुनुपर्ने दबाब बढेको छ । यद्यपि बैंकले भने प्रक्रिया पुर्‍याएर नै यस समूहलाई ऋण प्रवाह गरेको दाबी गरेको छ । राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंक स्रोतका अनुसार यस बैंकले यस बैंकले प्रवाह गरेको कर्जा असुली हुन नसकेपछि बारम्बार कर्जा चुक्ता गर्न आह्वान गरेको थियो । तर, कर्जा चुक्ता हुन नसकेपछि बैंकले एनजिएम इन्जिनीयरिङ एण्ड सेल्स प्रालिको धितोमा रहेको सम्पत्ति लिलाम गर्ने प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढाएको छ । बैंकले पर्सामा रहेको ५७ करोड ९७ लाख २१ हजार रुपैयाँ बराबरको जग्गा लिलामी प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाइसकेको छ । ज्योति समूहलाई दिइएको कर्जा र त्यसको उपयोगिताबारे बैंकले समेत गम्भिररुपमा लिएको बैंक स्रोतको भनाई छ । ‘हामीले नियमानुसार नै धितो मूल्यांकन गरेर कर्जा प्रवाह गरेका हौँ । तर, कर्जा दुरुपयोगबारे उठेका विषयहरूलाई गम्भिररुपमा लिएका छौँ’ राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंकका एक अधिकारीले भने । ज्योति समूहलाई कर्जा प्रवाह गरेको नेपाल बैंकले पनि नेपाल जनरल मार्केटिङ र ग्रान्ड सिटी क्लिनिक एन्ड हस्पिटलसहित चार वटा कम्पनीलाई कारबाही प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढाएको छ । उनीहरूले कर्जा भुक्तानी नगरेपछि बैंकले डा. रूप ज्योति, उनका छोरा अभिक ज्योति र छोरी सुरुचि ज्योतिको नाममा रहेका धितो सम्पत्ति जफत तथा लिलामी गर्न सार्वजनिक सूचना प्रकाशित गरिसकेको छ । यी बैंकहरुले कर्जा असुलीका लागि लिलामीको सूचना जारी गरेपनि ऋण चुक्ता हुन भने सकेको सकेको छैन । उता ज्योति समूह सम्बद्ध कम्पनीका लेखापरीक्षकले राय दिन अस्वीकार गरेको लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा कसरी कर्जा प्रवाह भयो भन्ने प्रश्न उठेको छ । बैंकहरुले यदि कमजोर धितो, लेखापरीक्षकबाट राय दिन अस्वीकृत प्रतिवेदन र त्यस पश्चात् बैंकले कर्जा असुली प्रक्रियामा खेलेको भूमिकाका आधारमा बैंक तथा सम्बद्ध कर्मचारीको काम कारबाही उपर भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ अनुसार छानबिन हुन सक्ने देखिन्छ । लामो समयदेखि ज्योति समूहले गर्दै आएको कर्जा दुरुपयोगको विषय सार्वजनिक हुँदा पनि नियामक निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकले कारबाहीको कदम चाल्न भने सकेको छैन । यसबारे केन्द्रीय बैंकले सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोत बतायो । राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोतले भन्यो, ‘वित्तीय क्षेत्रको स्थायित्व र सर्वसाधारणको निक्षेप संरक्षणमा केन्द्रीय बैंक प्रतिबद्ध छ । विभिन्न सञ्चार माध्यममा आएका समाचार र महालेखाको प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा बैंकहरूको सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ । गैरकानूनी रूपमा कर्जा प्रवाह गरेको भए कानूनी दायरामा ल्याउँछौँ ।’ सम्बन्धित समाचार Kathmandu. Questions have been raised about the role of two government banks in the illegal diversion of billions of rupees of loans taken from banks and financial institutions by Jyoti Group Chairman Dr. Roop Jyoti and his affiliated companies. The need for an investigation arose after the Office of the Auditor General officially entered the matter through a report and concluded that citizens' savings were put at risk and taxes were being evaded. The report of the Accountant General has now reached the Public Accounts Committee of the Federal Parliament. The report states that the government has been directed to investigate and take action against the transactions of companies involved in loan misuse and tax evasion in accordance with the prevailing provisions of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058 BS, the Banking Offences and Punishments Act, 2064 BS, and the Income Tax Act, 2058 BS, in cooperation and coordination with other investigative agencies of the state. Two government-owned banks, Rastriya Banijya Bank and Nepal Bank, are involved in this loan case. After the Accountant General declared the matter as null and void, questions have been raised about the role of the company concerned, the bank that invested the loan, and the regulatory body. Generally, the audit report is the main basis for disbursing loans to any company or organization. However, the issue of how these government banks approved loans worth billions based on the disputed audit report, on which the auditor of the Jyoti Group affiliated company refused to give an opinion, has come under debate. Pressure has increased on these two banks to investigate the role they played in the solid recovery process, even after it became public that loans were being given and loans were being misused despite weak collateral and a report deemed questionable by the auditors. However, the bank has claimed that it disbursed the loan to this group after completing the process. According to a source from the National Commercial Bank, the bank had repeatedly called for repayment of the loan after the loan disbursed by this bank could not be recovered. However, after the loan could not be repaid, the bank has moved forward with the process of auctioning the property mortgaged by NGM Engineering and Sales Pvt. Ltd. The bank has already moved forward with the auction process of land worth Rs 579.721 crore in Parsa. A bank source said that the bank has taken the loan given to the Jyoti group and its usefulness seriously. "We have disbursed the loan after evaluating the collateral as per the rules. However, we have taken the issues raised about loan misuse seriously," said an official of the National Commercial Bank. Nepal Bank, which has provided loans to the Jyoti group, has also initiated legal proceedings against four companies, including Nepal General Marketing and Grand City Clinic and Hospital. After they failed to repay the loans, the bank has issued a public notice to seize and auction the collateral in the names of Dr. Roop Jyoti, his son Abhik Jyoti, and daughter Suruchi Jyoti. Although these banks have issued notices of auctions for loan recovery, the loans have not been repaid. On the other hand, the question has been raised as to how the loans were disbursed based on the audit report of the Jyoti Group affiliated companies, which refused to give an opinion. If the banks have weak collateral, the auditor's report refusing to give an opinion, and the role played by the bank in the loan recovery process, it seems that the actions of the bank and its related employees may be investigated under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059 BS. Even after the issue of loan misuse by the Jyoti Group became public, the regulatory body Nepal Rastra Bank has not been able to take any action. The central bank is conducting a detailed investigation into the matter, a Rastra Bank source said. A Rastra Bank source said, 'The central bank is committed to the stability of the financial sector and the protection of deposits of the general public. A detailed investigation of the banks is being carried out based on news reports in various media outlets and the report of the Accountant General. If they have provided loans illegally, we will bring them under the legal ambit.' Related news

बैंकले कर्जा असुली प्रक्रियामा खेलेको भूमिकाका आधारमा बैंक तथा सम्बद्ध कर्मचारीको काम कारबाही उपर भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ अनुसार छानबिन हुन सक्ने देखिन्छ । लामो समयदेखि ज्योति समूहले गर्दै आएको कर्जा दुरुपयोगको विषय सार्वजनिक हुँदा पनि नियामक निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकले कारबाहीको कदम चाल्न भने सकेको छैन । यसबारे केन्द्रीय बैंकले सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोत बतायो । राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोतले भन्यो, ‘वित्तीय क्षेत्रको स्थायित्व र सर्वसाधारणको निक्षेप संरक्षणमा केन्द्रीय बैंक प्रतिबद्ध छ । विभिन्न सञ्चार माध्यममा आएका समाचार र महालेखाको प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा बैंकहरूको सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ । गैरकानूनी रूपमा कर्जा प्रवाह गरेको भए कानूनी दायरामा ल्याउँछौँ ।’ सम्बन्धित समाचार

काठमाडौं । ज्योति समूहका अध्यक्ष डा. रूप ज्योति र उनीसँग सम्बद्ध कम्पनीहरूले बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट लिएको अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ कर्जा गैरकानूनी रूपमा अन्यत्र प्रवाह गरी दुरुपयोग गरेको विषयमा दुई सरकारी बैंकको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न उठेको छ ।

महालेखापरीक्षकको कार्यालयले प्रतिवेदनमार्फत यो प्रकरणमा आधिकारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गर्दै नागरिकको बचत जोखिममा पारिएको र कर छली गरिएको निष्कर्ष निकालेपछि छानबिन गर्नुपर्ने स्थिति सिर्जना भएको हो ।

महालेखाको उक्त प्रतिवेदन अहिले संघीय संसद्को सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिमा पुगेको छ । प्रतिवेदनमा कर्जा दुरुपयोग र कर छलीमा संलग्न कम्पनीहरूको कारोबारलाई नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक ऐन, २०५८, बैंकिङ्ग कसुर तथा सजाय ऐन, २०६४ र आयकर ऐन, २०५८ का प्रचलित व्यवस्था अनुसार राज्यका अन्य अनुसन्धानकारी निकायहरूको सहयोग र समन्वयमा छानबिन गरी कारबाही गर्न सरकारलाई निर्देशन दिएको उल्लेख छ ।

यस कर्जा प्रकरणमा सरकारी स्वामित्वका दुई बैंकहरू राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंक र नेपाल बैंक जोडिएका छन् । महालेखाले यस विषयलाई बेरुजुका रूपमा समेत कायम गरेपछि सम्बन्धित कम्पनी, कर्जा लगानी गर्ने बैंक तथा नियामक निकायको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न उठेको छ ।

सामान्यतया, कुनै पनि कम्पनी वा संस्थालाई कर्जा प्रवाह गर्दा त्यसको लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदन मुख्य आधार हुन्छ । तर, ज्योति समूह सम्बद्ध कम्पनीका लेखापरीक्षकले राय दिन अस्वीकार गरेको विवादित लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदनकै आधारमा यी सरकारी बैंकहरूले कसरी अर्बौँ कर्जा स्वीकृत गरे भन्ने विषय बहसमा आएको छ ।

कमजोर धितो र लेखापरीक्षकले नै शंकास्पद ठहर्‍याएको प्रतिवेदन प्राप्त हुँदाहुँदै कर्जा दिनु र कर्जा दुरुपयोग भएको सार्वजनिक भइसक्दा पनि असुलीको ठोस प्रक्रियामा खेलेको भूमिकाका आधारमा यी दुई बैंकमाथी पनि छानबिन हुनुपर्ने दबाब बढेको छ ।

यद्यपि बैंकले भने प्रक्रिया पुर्‍याएर नै यस समूहलाई ऋण प्रवाह गरेको दाबी गरेको छ । राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंक स्रोतका अनुसार यस बैंकले यस बैंकले प्रवाह गरेको कर्जा असुली हुन नसकेपछि बारम्बार कर्जा चुक्ता गर्न आह्वान गरेको थियो । तर, कर्जा चुक्ता हुन नसकेपछि बैंकले एनजिएम इन्जिनीयरिङ एण्ड सेल्स प्रालिको धितोमा रहेको सम्पत्ति लिलाम गर्ने प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढाएको छ । बैंकले पर्सामा रहेको ५७ करोड ९७ लाख २१ हजार रुपैयाँ बराबरको जग्गा लिलामी प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाइसकेको छ ।

ज्योति समूहलाई दिइएको कर्जा र त्यसको उपयोगिताबारे बैंकले समेत गम्भिररुपमा लिएको बैंक स्रोतको भनाई छ । ‘हामीले नियमानुसार नै धितो मूल्यांकन गरेर कर्जा प्रवाह गरेका हौँ । तर, कर्जा दुरुपयोगबारे उठेका विषयहरूलाई गम्भिररुपमा लिएका छौँ’ राष्ट्रिय वाणिज्य बैंकका एक अधिकारीले भने ।

ज्योति समूहलाई कर्जा प्रवाह गरेको नेपाल बैंकले पनि नेपाल जनरल मार्केटिङ र ग्रान्ड सिटी क्लिनिक एन्ड हस्पिटलसहित चार वटा कम्पनीलाई कारबाही प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढाएको छ । उनीहरूले कर्जा भुक्तानी नगरेपछि बैंकले डा. रूप ज्योति, उनका छोरा अभिक ज्योति र छोरी सुरुचि ज्योतिको नाममा रहेका धितो सम्पत्ति जफत तथा लिलामी गर्न सार्वजनिक सूचना प्रकाशित गरिसकेको छ ।

यी बैंकहरुले कर्जा असुलीका लागि लिलामीको सूचना जारी गरेपनि ऋण चुक्ता हुन भने सकेको सकेको छैन । उता ज्योति समूह सम्बद्ध कम्पनीका लेखापरीक्षकले राय दिन अस्वीकार गरेको लेखापरीक्षण प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा कसरी कर्जा प्रवाह भयो भन्ने प्रश्न उठेको छ । बैंकहरुले यदि कमजोर धितो, लेखापरीक्षकबाट राय दिन अस्वीकृत प्रतिवेदन र त्यस पश्चात् बैंकले कर्जा असुली प्रक्रियामा खेलेको भूमिकाका आधारमा बैंक तथा सम्बद्ध कर्मचारीको काम कारबाही उपर भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ अनुसार छानबिन हुन सक्ने देखिन्छ ।

लामो समयदेखि ज्योति समूहले गर्दै आएको कर्जा दुरुपयोगको विषय सार्वजनिक हुँदा पनि नियामक निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकले कारबाहीको कदम चाल्न भने सकेको छैन । यसबारे केन्द्रीय बैंकले सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोत बतायो ।

राष्ट्र बैंक स्रोतले भन्यो, ‘वित्तीय क्षेत्रको स्थायित्व र सर्वसाधारणको निक्षेप संरक्षणमा केन्द्रीय बैंक प्रतिबद्ध छ । विभिन्न सञ्चार माध्यममा आएका समाचार र महालेखाको प्रतिवेदनका आधारमा बैंकहरूको सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ । गैरकानूनी रूपमा कर्जा प्रवाह गरेको भए कानूनी दायरामा ल्याउँछौँ ।’

Kathmandu. Questions have been raised about the role of two government banks in the illegal diversion of billions of rupees of loans taken from banks and financial institutions by Jyoti Group Chairman Dr. Roop Jyoti and his affiliated companies. The need for an investigation arose after the Office of the Auditor General officially entered the matter through a report and concluded that citizens' savings were put at risk and taxes were being evaded. The report of the Accountant General has now reached the Public Accounts Committee of the Federal Parliament. The report states that the government has been directed to investigate and take action against the transactions of companies involved in loan misuse and tax evasion in accordance with the prevailing provisions of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058 BS, the Banking Offences and Punishments Act, 2064 BS, and the Income Tax Act, 2058 BS, in cooperation and coordination with other investigative agencies of the state. Two government-owned banks, Rastriya Banijya Bank and Nepal Bank, are involved in this loan case. After the Accountant General declared the matter as null and void, questions have been raised about the role of the company concerned, the bank that invested the loan, and the regulatory body. Generally, the audit report is the main basis for disbursing loans to any company or organization. However, the issue of how these government banks approved loans worth billions based on the disputed audit report, on which the auditor of the Jyoti Group affiliated company refused to give an opinion, has come under debate. Pressure has increased on these two banks to investigate the role they played in the solid recovery process, even after it became public that loans were being given and loans were being misused despite weak collateral and a report deemed questionable by the auditors. However, the bank has claimed that it disbursed the loan to this group after completing the process. According to a source from the National Commercial Bank, the bank had repeatedly called for repayment of the loan after the loan disbursed by this bank could not be recovered. However, after the loan could not be repaid, the bank has moved forward with the process of auctioning the property mortgaged by NGM Engineering and Sales Pvt. Ltd. The bank has already moved forward with the auction process of land worth Rs 579.721 crore in Parsa. A bank source said that the bank has taken the loan given to the Jyoti group and its usefulness seriously. "We have disbursed the loan after evaluating the collateral as per the rules. However, we have taken the issues raised about loan misuse seriously," said an official of the National Commercial Bank. Nepal Bank, which has provided loans to the Jyoti group, has also initiated legal proceedings against four companies, including Nepal General Marketing and Grand City Clinic and Hospital. After they failed to repay the loans, the bank has issued a public notice to seize and auction the collateral in the names of Dr. Roop Jyoti, his son Abhik Jyoti, and daughter Suruchi Jyoti. Although these banks have issued notices of auctions for loan recovery, the loans have not been repaid. On the other hand, the question has been raised as to how the loans were disbursed based on the audit report of the Jyoti Group affiliated companies, which refused to give an opinion. If the banks have weak collateral, the auditor's report refusing to give an opinion, and the role played by the bank in the loan recovery process, it seems that the actions of the bank and its related employees may be investigated under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059 BS. Even after the issue of loan misuse by the Jyoti Group became public, the regulatory body Nepal Rastra Bank has not been able to take any action. The central bank is conducting a detailed investigation into the matter, a Rastra Bank source said. A Rastra Bank source said, 'The central bank is committed to the stability of the financial sector and the protection of deposits of the general public. A detailed investigation of the banks is being carried out based on news reports in various media outlets and the report of the Accountant General. If they have provided loans illegally, we will bring them under the legal ambit.' Related news
